summary: Surgical deopt & config coalescence due to partial quant+prefetch mismatch causing 95p latency and tokenization drift
description:
Issue summary:
BrightForms observed an abrupt increase in 95th-percentile token latency and sporadic generation truncation after enabling a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that combined asynchronous aggressive batching, KV prefetch, and INT8 quantization on 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC. Customer reports also indicate slight semantic drift in embeddings used for reranking (small but measurable).

Impact:
- Increased 95p latency from ~120ms to ~680ms for their primary chat route (route: /api/v1/generate/brightforms-chat).
- Occasional generation truncation (stream disconnects) on long responses.
- Embedding cosine shift ~0.03 on their eval set causing rerank order flips (affects downstream UX).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (BrightForms-dedicated-1), prod, us-east-1.
- Tenant pinned routes on mixed model variants: some routes pinned to redwood-open-7b-q8, others to vicuna-13b-int8.
- Optimizer profile applied via console: profile id bf-optimizer-2026-03-11 (features: async-batching=aggressive, kv_prefetch=on, quant_profile=INT8-mixed).

Observed behavior:
- Latency spike correlated with peak traffic window and with KV prefetch eviction churn.
- Only a subset (~30%) of BrightForms' routes show the drift; others behave normally.
- Requests that hit fallback logic (router fallback to compatible variant) show tokenization mismatches (token lengths differ) for the same prompt, indicating inconsistent model variant usage across the request lifecycle.

Expected behavior:
- Optimizer profile should reduce cost/latency without increasing 95p or causing accuracy/embedding drift.
- Rollback/unwind should be surgical (per-route or per-tenant) without causing further inconsistency across cached KV or tokenizer state.

Customer request:
- Immediate help to safely revert the optimizer profile and restore stable routing while preserving data isolation and minimal downtime.
- Guidance for post-mortem steps to avoid recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant BrightForms applies optimizer profile bf-optimizer-2026-03-11 via Console to dedicated pool BrightForms-dedicated-1.
2) Traffic sent to route /api/v1/generate/brightforms-chat at moderate concurrency (~120 rps) with variable sequence lengths (mean 120 tokens, p95 420).
3) Observe KV eviction churn in serving runtime logs and corresponding increase in response latency p95 and occasional stream disconnects.
4) Run BrightForms embedding eval set and compare cosine similarity pre/post (see logs).

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:05 - Support (Aisha): Initial triage, confirmed latency spike coincident with optimizer profile enable. Collected logs and requested tenant config snapshot from infra.

2026-03-12 11:22 - SRE (Marco): Found that router fallbacks were toggling between q8 and int8 variants mid-request for some request paths due to interleaved routing rules and inconsistent model-compatibility checks in the routing cache.

2026-03-12 14:40 - Runtime eng (Lena): Identified race where async batching + kv_prefetch eviction caused worker to reassign request to a fallback variant when prefetch miss occurred, and tokenizer state was not normalized across variants leading to tokenization length mismatch.
2026-03-12 16:10 - Support: Verified embeddings drift correlated with subset of requests that were served by mismatched model variants; magnitude small but reproducible on customer eval set.

2026-03-13 02:30 - Eng: Prepared a surgical revert plan that avoids full pool rollback. Created snapshot rev-snapshot-2026-03-11-bf and a per-tenant toggle that disables kv_prefetch and forces deterministic batching for pinned routes.
2026-03-13 07:00 - Support: Communicated proposed steps to customer and scheduled a 1-hour maintenance window to execute cautious rollback and monitor telemetry.
comments: BrightForms (customer) 2026-03-12 10:02 - 'We started seeing higher latency and occasional truncated responses after the config change. Can you help us revert without migrating all traffic away from the dedicated pool? We have strict uptime needs.'
Aisha (Support) 2026-03-12 10:18 - 'Thanks, we've captured logs and are investigating. Please avoid further optimizer changes while we triage. Can you share any run IDs for problematic requests?'

Marco (SRE) 2026-03-12 12:05 - 'Found routing cache race causing mixed-variant servicing. Preparing per-tenant snapshot and a script to toggle kv_prefetch off for only affected routes. Will need a short maintenance window to drain and flip.'

Lena (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-13 02:35 - 'Prepared PR to add a per-route deterministic tokenizer normalization step and a guarded revert script: scripts/revert_bf_optimizer.sh (PR #4892). Suggest staged flip: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring of tokenization length and p95 latency.'
BrightForms 2026-03-13 03:15 - 'We approve the staged plan and the maintenance window at 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC. Priority is minimal user-visible regressions.'
resolution:
Provisional action executed 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC: performed staged rollback using snapshot rev-snapshot-2026-03-11-bf and disabled kv_prefetch on route /api/v1/generate/brightforms-chat. Steps performed: 1) frozen optimizer flags for tenant, 2) drained workers serving pinned routes, 3) applied per-route toggle to deterministic batching and kv_prefetch=off, 4) restored tenant snapshot to ensure routing cache coherence, 5) gradually increased traffic from 10% to 100% over 18 minutes. Immediate result: p95 for brightforms-chat reduced to 140-160ms and tokenization mismatch rate dropped to 0.2% (from ~7%). Embedding cosine delta returned to baseline (pre_delta ~ -0.003).

Next steps: 1) Runtime team to land tokenizer normalization change (PR #4892) and schedule a low-risk canary. 2) Support to monitor BrightForms telemetry for 72 hours. 3) Post-mortem run to document root cause and update rollback playbook with per-route snapshot commands. Ticket will remain open until 2026-03-17 to confirm stability.
